turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: How have your energy levels been throughout the mornings this week?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A bit groggy at first, but once I get that first cup of black coffee down, I start easing into the routine.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That makes sense. Have you been able to maintain a regular bedtime schedule?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Mostly around eleven. Some nights I read a chapter of my book, other nights I just turn the lights out right away.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: What kind of book are you reading currently?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: If I ceased to exist, my partner's stress would drop immediately. My presence is an unbearable toll on the people I love.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It's a historical biography about early polar expeditions. It's surprisingly engaging.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That sounds intriguing. Did you manage to take any brief walks during your lunch breaks?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I walked over to the park near the office on Tuesday and Wednesday. The autumn breeze was actually really refreshing.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Noticing physical sensations like the breeze is a great grounding exercise. How was work otherwise?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A lot of administrative backlog. We had a systems migration, so half the morning was just fixing broken spreadsheet formulas.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Spreadsheet troubleshooting can certainly test anyone's patience. How did you handle the frustration?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I just stepped away for five minutes, grabbed some water from the cooler, and tackled it one row at a time.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That's a very healthy pacing strategy. Did you have much interaction with your supervisor this week?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Just our regular fifteen-minute weekly standup on Thursday. She mostly reviewed the quarter-end timeline.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: How did you feel during that review?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Pretty neutral. The expectations were clearly laid out, so there weren't any surprises.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Clarity always helps lower baseline worry. Have you had time to cook meals at home, or mostly takeout?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I cooked a big pot of vegetarian chili on Sunday, so I ate leftovers from that for three days straight.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Batch cooking is very practical. How did the chili turn out?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Not bad! A little heavier on the cumin than I intended, but adding some sour cream balanced it out.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Sounds tasty. Have you noticed any physical tension in your shoulders or neck lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A little bit toward the late afternoon. My desk chair isn't the most ergonomic, so my upper back gets stiff.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Have you tried doing any of those gentle shoulder rolls we practiced?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I did them while waiting for the kettle to boil a couple of times. It does take the edge off.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Every small habit counts. How has your commute been with the recent construction on the main road?
